blocks.content: Mr. Alvarez has been asking me questions I don't want to answer since the second week I started coming here. Not intrusive ones. Just — precise ones. The kind that find the exact thing you were hoping not to discuss.
New subject?
He nodded at the sketchbook.
Practice.
Practice.
He said it the way someone repeats a word when they know it isn't the real word.
Figures. I practice figures.
Of course.
He set down his rag and leaned on the counter.
You know what I put in that coffee?
Two sugars.
Two sugars. Because bitterness should only exist in art.
I had heard that line before. He said it every time he handed me the cup, which meant either he thought I kept forgetting it, or he thought it kept being true.
I think he thought it kept being true.
You ever think about painting something you didn't commission?
All the time.
And?
And then rent is a thing that exists.
He made a small sound — not quite agreement, not quite disagreement. The sound for when someone is right about the facts but wrong about something larger.

I used to think I'd know, eventually. What the painting was. The one I actually wanted to make, versus the ones people paid me to make. Most artists I'd read about talked about it like a conversation — you work toward it, it works toward you, and eventually you meet somewhere in the middle.
So far the conversation had been mostly me talking to an empty room.
